input.cause: The refusals were true and the guard did what its text said. In the exp3 task (step 8) the model sent steps.1.minutes = 25 (rise) and steps.2.minutes = 30 (decay). It filed the justification of the decay duration, tau = V/Qe = 30 min, under the path steps.1.minutes, and filed nothing for steps.2.minutes. The guard keys a justification by path, so it said "the justification says 30, what you sent sets 25" and "steps.2.minutes = 30 has no justification". On the retry the model gave steps.1.minutes the value 25 with a rise derivation and added steps.2.minutes, so the guard accepted it. The first retry fixed it every time because the model mis-keyed its own constant, not because it learned a hidden rule. The path-keying rule is already in what the model reads: justify.ts and the brief both say a justification names its constant by its path. The class is model-error: a mismatch between the model's own step values and its own justification paths. It is not a contract gap, and the rule was not learned by refusal. The same refusal also carried other points (safety constants cited by a made-up id instead of a fact id), which are a separate form. Each of the three tasks showed the same mis-keying of steps.1.minutes.

predictions.alternative: the guard refused with a false reason (the justification was right and the guard compared the wrong constants)

input.summary: Diagnosis accepted by the guard as diagnoses/diag-fcd5af1afd1d.json (sha256 f64cf997...9023). All 5 predictions were confirmed true by the harness. The lead is about the form "justification: *: the justification says #, what you sent sets #" (rule JUSTIFIED_VALUE_MISMATCH). I did not re-read the cause text, so this summary rests on the harness's own confirmations rather than on the accepted file. At step 8 of task exp3-baseline/t-2026-09-29-0010 the model sent 25 at /steps/[n=1]/minutes, but its justification for steps.1.minutes said 30, which was a derived time constant tau=V/Qe. The refusal also named other problems: unjustified safety constants, and no justification at all for steps.2.minutes. The guard's message says the justification value and the sent value must agree. The model corrected by changing the justification's value and reference to match the step it had sent (25 min). It did so each time at the first retry, in all 3 tasks. This repeated correction is a response to a refusal that the texts the model read did state; the rule is stated today in harness/core/justify.ts. The lead's reading as a rule "learned" is therefore a normal correction, and the lead is still current.
